name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MCQ_Q45 - Synthesis of fluorobenzene via diazonium fluoroborate

questiontext.text: Fluorobenzene is prepared by treating benzenediazonium chloride with fluoroboric acid (\(\mathrm{HBF_4}\)) to precipitate benzenediazonium fluoroborate, followed by thermal decomposition. What are the products of this thermal decomposition?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the reaction sequence
Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with \(\mathrm{HBF_4}\) to precipitate water-insoluble benzenediazonium fluoroborate: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+ Cl^- + HBF_4 \rightarrow C_6H_5N_2^+ BF_4^- + HCl}\).

Step 2: Trace the thermal decomposition
Upon dry heating, the fluoroborate salt undergoes decomposition: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+ BF_4^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_5F + BF_3 + N_2}\).

Conclusion:
Thermal decomposition yields fluorobenzene, \(\mathrm{BF_3}\), and \(\mathrm{N_2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MCQ_Q46 - Reduction of diazonium salts to benzene

questiontext.text: Benzenediazonium chloride can be reduced to benzene by treatment with hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) or ethanol. During these reactions, what oxidation products are formed from \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\) and ethanol, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Write the redox equation with hypophosphorous acid
\(\mathrm{ArN_2^+ Cl^- + H_3PO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow ArH + N_2 + H_3PO_3 + HCl}\). Here, hypophosphorous acid (oxidation state +1) is oxidised to phosphorous acid (oxidation state +3).

Step 2: Write the redox equation with ethanol
\(\mathrm{ArN_2^+ Cl^- + CH_3CH_2OH \rightarrow ArH + N_2 + CH_3CHO + HCl}\). Here, ethanol is oxidised to ethanal (acetaldehyde).

Conclusion:
The respective oxidation products are phosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)) and ethanal (\(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MCQ_Q47 - Azo coupling reactions forming coloured dyes

questiontext.text: Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes electrophilic coupling with phenol in basic medium and with aniline in mildly acidic medium to produce coloured azo dyes. What are the names and colours of these dyes, respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine coupling with phenol
In basic medium (\(\mathrm{pH\ 9-10}\)), phenol forms phenoxide ion, which is intensely activated and couples at its para position with benzenediazonium chloride to yield \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange dye.

Step 2: Examine coupling with aniline
In mildly acidic medium (\(\mathrm{pH\ 4-5}\)), aniline couples at its para position with benzenediazonium chloride to yield \(p\)-aminoazobenzene, a yellow dye.

Conclusion:
The products are \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye) and \(p\)-aminoazobenzene (yellow dye).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MCQ_Q48 - Multistep conversion of aniline to tribromobenzene

questiontext.text: Which sequence of reactions correctly accomplishes the conversion of aniline into 1,3,5-tribromobenzene?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Exploit the activating directing effect of the amino group
Treating aniline with bromine water causes bromination at all available ortho and para positions (carbons 2, 4, and 6), yielding 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

Step 2: Convert the amino group into a leaving diazonium group
Subjecting 2,4,6-tribromoaniline to diazotisation with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\) at \(273 - 278\,\mathrm{K}\) converts the \(-\mathrm{NH_2}\) group into \(-\mathrm{N_2^+ Cl^-}\), producing 2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Step 3: Remove the diazonium group reductively
Treating 2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride with hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) in water replaces the diazonium group with hydrogen, leaving bromine atoms at the 1, 3, and 5 positions to give 1,3,5-tribromobenzene.

Conclusion:
The sequence is bromination with \(\mathrm{Br_2 / H_2O}\), diazotisation with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2 / HCl}\), and reductive deamination with \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2 / H_2O}\).

answer.text: Direct bromination of benzene with \(\mathrm{Br_2 / FeBr_3}\) \(\rightarrow\) nitration \(\rightarrow\) reduction with \(\mathrm{Sn / HCl}\)
Diazotisation with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2 / HCl}\) \(\rightarrow\) reaction with \(\mathrm{Cu_2Br_2 / HBr}\) \(\rightarrow\) bromination with \(\mathrm{Br_2 / Fe}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q01 - Hybridization and geometry of nitrogen in amines

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In amines, the nitrogen atom is \(sp^3\) hybridised and the geometry is pyramidal.

Statement II: Due to the presence of an unshared pair of electrons, the \(\mathrm{C-N-E}\) bond angle (where \(\mathrm{E}\) is \(\mathrm{C}\) or \(\mathrm{H}\)) is less than \(109.5^\circ\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The nitrogen atom of an amine possesses five valence electrons. Three of these electrons participate in \(\sigma\) bonding with carbon or hydrogen atoms, while the fourth orbital accommodates an unshared electron pair, corresponding to \(sp^3\) hybridization.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that nitrogen in amines adopts \(sp^3\) hybridization with a pyramidal molecular shape is accurate because the three bonding orbitals point toward the base of a trigonal pyramid with the unshared pair occupying the apex.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that the bond angle is compressed below the ideal tetrahedral value of \(109.5^\circ\) (measuring, for instance, \(108^\circ\) in trimethylamine) is accurate as lone pair-bond pair repulsions exceed bond pair-bond pair repulsions.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both the structural hybridization description and the lone-pair-induced bond angle reduction are accurate. Concluding assessment: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q02 - Reduction of nitrobenzene to produce benzenamine efficiently

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Reduction of nitro compounds using iron scrap and hydrochloric acid is preferred industrially over tin and hydrochloric acid.

Statement II: The reduction requires equimolar amounts of hydrochloric acid because \(\mathrm{FeCl}_2\) formed is completely unreactive with water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The preparation of primary aromatic amines from nitro compounds involves reduction with active metals in the presence of an aqueous mineral acid.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that reduction with iron scrap and hydrochloric acid is preferred over other metals is accurate because iron is readily available, inexpensive, and economically advantageous.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that stoichiometric amounts of hydrochloric acid are required because iron(II) chloride does not react with water is inaccurate. In reality, the \(\mathrm{FeCl}_2\) formed during the reaction undergoes hydrolysis to release hydrochloric acid, meaning only a small catalytic amount of \(\mathrm{HCl}\) is needed to initiate the reaction.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first proposition is chemically accurate, whereas the explanation regarding the non-reactivity of iron(II) chloride is false. Concluding assessment: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q03 - Preparation of primary amines by Gabriel synthesis

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aromatic primary amines such as aniline can be prepared readily by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

Statement II: Potassium phthalimide undergoes nucleophilic substitution with primary alkyl halides to yield \(N\)-alkylphthalimides.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is a specialized laboratory method used to produce pure primary amines through nucleophilic substitution on an organohalogen substrate.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that aromatic primary amines like aniline can be prepared by this method is inaccurate because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion under standard conditions due to resonance stabilization and partial double-bond character of the carbon-halogen bond.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that potassium phthalimide reacts with primary alkyl halides to give \(N\)-alkylphthalimides is accurate as the phthalimide nitrogen acts as a strong nucleophile in an \(S_N2\) displacement.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claim regarding the preparation of aromatic primary amines is invalid, whereas the reaction mechanism with alkyl halides is valid. Concluding assessment: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q04 - Hoffmann bromamide degradation of primary amides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction converts an amide into a primary amine containing one more carbon atom than the starting amide.

Statement II: In Hoffmann bromamide degradation, an alkyl or aryl group migrates from the nitrogen atom to the carbonyl carbon atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction converts a primary carboxamide into a primary amine by treatment with bromine in aqueous or ethanolic sodium hydroxide solution.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that the resulting amine contains one more carbon atom than the reactant amide is inaccurate because the carbonyl carbon is lost as carbonate ion (\(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3\)), producing an amine with one fewer carbon atom.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that migration proceeds from the nitrogen atom to the carbonyl carbon is inaccurate because the alkyl or aryl group actually migrates from the carbonyl carbon to the electron-deficient nitrogen intermediate during rearrangement.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both propositions contradict the established stoichiometry and mechanism of the reaction. Concluding assessment: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

The assertion that primary amines undergo intermolecular hydrogen bonding through their two polar \(\mathrm{N-H}\) bonds, whereas tertiary amines cannot undergo self-associated hydrogen bonding due to the absence of \(\mathrm{N-H}\) bonds, is accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both the observed relative boiling points and the structural rationale involving hydrogen bonding are accurate. Concluding assessment: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q06 - Chemical tests for distinguishing aliphatic amines

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aliphatic primary amines on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide produce foul-smelling isocyanides.

Statement II: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid at 273–278 K to form stable diazonium salts that can be isolated as crystalline solids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Primary aliphatic amines exhibit characteristic electrophilic and elimination pathways when treated with chloroform in base or with nitrous acid.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that primary aliphatic amines react with chloroform and ethanolic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) to yield foul-smelling carbylamines (isocyanides) is accurate, serving as the basis of the carbylamine test.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that aliphatic primary amines form stable diazonium salts at 273–278 K that can be isolated is inaccurate because aliphatic diazonium salts are highly unstable and decompose quantitatively to release dinitrogen gas along with a mixture of alcohols, alkenes, and alkyl halides.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The description of the carbylamine reaction is valid, whereas the claim regarding the stability of aliphatic diazonium salts is invalid. Concluding assessment: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q07 - Sulphonamide solubility behavior in Hinsberg test

questiontext.text:

Statement I: The sulphonamide obtained from the reaction of diethylamine with benzenesulphonyl chloride dissolves readily in aqueous potassium hydroxide.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that tertiary amines react with benzenesulphonyl chloride to yield clear solutions that precipitate upon adding acid is inaccurate because tertiary amines have no hydrogen on nitrogen and do not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride under these conditions.

Step 4: Final Conclusion

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT_Q08 - Activation and substitution control in aniline

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Treatment of aniline with bromine water at room temperature yields exclusively 4-bromoaniline without any polybromination.

Statement II: Protection of the amino group of aniline by acetylation moderates its reactivity because the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalized to the carbonyl oxygen through resonance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The amino group in aniline is exceptionally activating toward electrophilic aromatic substitution due to strong resonance donation of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring.

Step 2: Analysis of the First Proposition
The assertion that bromine water produces only 4-bromoaniline is inaccurate because the activating power of the unprotected amino group is so high that substitution occurs simultaneously at all ortho and para positions, yielding a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

Step 3: Analysis of the Second Proposition
The assertion that acetylation to form acetanilide moderates ring activation is accurate because the nitrogen lone pair participates in resonance with the adjacent carbonyl oxygen, reducing its availability for donation into the aromatic ring.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement regarding mono-bromination by bromine water is invalid, whereas the resonance explanation of amino-group protection is valid. Concluding assessment: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Nomenclature and physical classification of aliphatic amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structure, classification, and physical properties of amines:

Statement I: In the IUPAC nomenclature system, primary aliphatic amines are designated as alkanamines by replacing the suffix 'e' of the alkane with 'amine'.

Statement II: The lower aliphatic amines, such as methanamine and ethanamine, are gases with a characteristic fishy odour.

Statement III: Quaternary ammonium salts contain four alkyl or aryl groups attached to nitrogen and carry a net negative formal charge.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amines are formally derived from ammonia by replacing hydrogen atoms with alkyl or aryl groups, classified as primary, secondary, tertiary, or quaternary ammonium derivatives.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that primary aliphatic amines are named as alkanamines in the IUPAC system by replacing the terminal 'e' of alkane with 'amine' (e.g., methanamine for \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2\)) is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that lower aliphatic amines with one or two carbon atoms exist as gases at ambient temperatures and possess fishy odours is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that quaternary ammonium salts possess a net negative charge is incorrect because the nitrogen atom shares four electron pairs to form four covalent bonds with carbon groups, resulting in a formal positive charge on the quaternary nitrogen (\(\mathrm{R}_4\mathrm{N}^+\)).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statements I and II are correct, whereas Statement III is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Aqueous phase basicity factors of substituted amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the basicity of aliphatic amines in aqueous solution:

Statement I: In the gaseous phase, the basic strength of alkyl-substituted amines increases strictly in the order: \(\mathrm{NH}_3 < 1^\circ < 2^\circ < 3^\circ\).

Statement II: In aqueous solution, the basic strength of methyl-substituted amines follows the order: \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 > (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH}_3\).

Statement III: The conjugate cation of a tertiary amine undergoes greater hydration stabilization via hydrogen bonding with water than the conjugate cation of a primary amine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The basic strength of amines in aqueous media is governed by a cooperative interplay between the inductive effect of alkyl groups, steric hindrance to protonation, and hydration stabilization of the resulting ammonium cations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that the gas-phase basicity order increases monotonically from primary to secondary to tertiary amines (\(\mathrm{NH}_3 < 1^\circ < 2^\circ < 3^\circ\)) due solely to the additive \(+I\) electron-releasing inductive effect of alkyl groups is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that methyl-substituted amines in aqueous solution follow the order secondary > primary > tertiary > ammonia (\((\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{NH}_2 > (\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH}_3\)) is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that the conjugate cation of a tertiary amine undergoes greater hydration stabilization than that of a primary amine is incorrect because the substituted ammonium ion of a primary amine (\(\mathrm{RNH}_3^+\)) possesses three hydrogen atoms available for hydrogen bonding with water molecules, whereas the tertiary cation (\(\mathrm{R}_3\mathrm{NH}^+\)) possesses only one such hydrogen atom, making hydration stabilization greatest for primary and least for tertiary cations.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statements I and II are correct, whereas Statement III is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Differentiation reactions for primary and secondary amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the chemical differentiation of amines:

Statement I: Both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines produce foul-smelling isocyanides when heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide.

Statement II: Secondary amines react with benzenesulphonyl chloride to yield \(N,N\)-dialkylbenzenesulphonamides that dissolve in aqueous sodium hydroxide.

Statement III: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to liberate dinitrogen gas quantitatively, a reaction utilized in the estimation of amino acids and proteins.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diagnostic chemical tests for amines depend on functional group transformations specific to the number of active hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines undergo the carbylamine reaction upon heating with \(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\) and ethanolic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) to form foul-smelling isocyanides is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that secondary amines form sulphonamides that dissolve in aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) is incorrect because the product \(N,N\)-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide lacks any acidic hydrogen atom on the nitrogen atom and is therefore insoluble in aqueous alkali.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to yield unstable diazonium intermediates that break down with quantitative liberation of dinitrogen gas (used analytically to quantify amino acids and proteins) is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statements I and III are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Synthetic applications of benzenediazonium chloride reactions

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding arenediazonium salts and the synthetic chemistry of aniline derivatives:

Statement I: Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is insoluble in water and remains stable at room temperature.

Statement II: Reduction of benzenediazonium chloride to benzene can be achieved by heating with hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\)) or with ethanol.

Statement III: Coupling reaction of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol is carried out in basic medium to produce \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange azo dye.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arenediazonium salts serve as versatile synthetic intermediates that undergo displacement of the diazonium group by nucleophiles or coupling with activated aromatic substrates to form azo dyes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that benzenediazonium fluoroborate (\(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{N}_2^+\mathrm{BF}_4^-\)) is water-insoluble and stable at ambient temperature is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{PO}_2\)) or ethanol acts as a mild reducing agent to reduce arenediazonium salts to parent arenes (while themselves being oxidized to phosphorous acid and ethanal, respectively) is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that benzenediazonium chloride undergoes an electrophilic aromatic coupling reaction with phenol in alkaline medium (forming phenoxide ion to increase ring electron density) at the para position to yield the orange dye \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
All three statements are factually and mechanistically accurate. Concluding assessment: I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT4_Q01 - Synthetic methods and basic characteristics of amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the synthesis and basicity of amines:

Statement I: Reduction of nitriles with lithium aluminium hydride (\(\mathrm{LiAlH}_4\)) or catalytic hydrogenation yields primary amines containing one carbon atom more than the starting alkyl halide used to prepare the nitrile.

Statement II: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis readily produces high yields of pure aromatic primary amines like aniline.

Statement III: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia in aqueous solution because alkyl groups possess a \(+I\) inductive effect.

Statement IV: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because the lone pair of electrons on nitrogen is delocalized over the aromatic ring through resonance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The preparation and relative basicity of amines are dictated by carbon-chain transformations, nucleophilic substitution feasibility, and the electronic environment (inductive vs. resonance delocalization) of the nitrogen lone pair.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that reduction of nitriles using \(\mathrm{LiAlH}_4\) or catalytic hydrogenation produces primary amines with an ascent of the series (incorporating the nitrile carbon) is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that aromatic primary amines such as aniline can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is incorrect because aryl halides fail to undergo bimolecular nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion under standard conditions.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia in aqueous solution due to the electron-releasing \(+I\) effect of alkyl groups, which stabilizes the alkylammonium cation, is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement IV
The assertion that aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because its nitrogen lone pair enters into resonance conjugation with the benzene ring (rendering it less accessible for protonation) is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements I, III, and IV are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I, III and IV only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT4_Q02 - Chemical reactions and diazonium coupling of amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the reactions of amines and diazonium salts:

Statement I: Primary aliphatic and aromatic amines react with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide to produce intensely foul-smelling isocyanides.

Statement II: The product obtained from the reaction of a primary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride contains an acidic hydrogen and dissolves in aqueous potassium hydroxide.

Statement III: Direct nitration of aniline with a nitrating mixture gives exclusively the ortho- and para-nitro derivatives without any meta-substituted product.

Statement IV: Coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol in a weakly alkaline medium takes place at the para position to form \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactions of amines and diazonium salts encompass electrophilic substitutions, nucleophilic additions/eliminations, and azo coupling reactions dependent on medium acidity and resonance activation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that primary aliphatic and aromatic amines undergo the carbylamine reaction upon heating with chloroform and ethanolic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) to form isocyanides is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that the Hinsberg reaction of a primary amine yields an \(N\)-alkylbenzenesulphonamide with an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen that dissolves in aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\) is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that direct nitration of aniline yields exclusively ortho- and para-products is incorrect because in strongly acidic media, aniline protonates to form the meta-directing anilinium ion, producing a significant yield (47%) of \(m\)-nitroaniline.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement IV
The assertion that benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol at the para position in mildly alkaline medium (pH 9–10) to generate the orange dye \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements I, II, and IV are correct, whereas Statement III is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I, II and IV only are correct.
